# Lua API reference

Everything a NetherForge script can call. Scripts are Lua 5.4. New to scripting NetherForge? Start with [Your first script](../guide/first-script.md) and [Scripting basics](../guide/scripting.md), then come back here to look things up.

Calls on `nf` and its namespaces use a dot (`nf.players.online()`); calls on a handle, like a player or a centity, use a colon (`player:send_message("hi")`).

## Basics

How scripts run, how events work, and the rules every name in the API follows.

- [Scripts](scripts.md): centity, menu, dialog, item and block scripts and modules, and the globals each gets
- [Events](events.md): how `:on` works, and every event each class has
- [Tables](types.md): event payloads, option tables and the records functions return
- [Naming rules](naming.md): how every name in the API is formed, so you can guess one you have not seen
- [Coordinate spaces](spaces.md): which space each position is in, and how to convert between them
- [Names across packages](packages.md): how a script names its own package's things and the packages' it depends on, and how names read back

## Core

Events, timers, tasks, saved data and the server itself.

- [nf](nf.md): Everything outside the script itself
- [Task](task.md): What `nf.task`, `nf.after` and `nf.every` return: a task that may be waiting, or a callback waiting to run
- [Subscription](subscription.md): What `:on` and `:once` return: one handler listening for one event on one handle (or on `nf`)
- [nf.server](nf.server.md): The server itself: its clock, its performance, its version, its settings (players, message of the day, whitelist), and saying or running things as the console
- [nf.commands](nf.commands.md): Slash commands a module adds to the server for as long as it runs, with typed arguments, tab completion and usage messages from their declaration
- [Sender](sender.md): Whoever ran a command: a player or the console
- [nf.schedule](nf.schedule.md): Runs a function at a time of day, every day or week, or by a cron expression: real time, as opposed to ticks (`nf.after`, `nf.every`)
- [Schedule](schedule.md): What `nf.schedule.daily`, `weekly` and `cron` return: a schedule that will run at its next time, until it is cancelled or its script unloads

## Centities and effects

Your own entities, the particle effects and cutscenes made in the editor.

- [nf.centities](nf.centities.md): Centity instances: spawning new ones and finding live ones
- [Centity](centity.md): One spawned centity: `this` in the centity's script, and what `nf.centities.spawn`, `nf.centities.get` and `nf.centities.all` return
- [Node](node.md): One node of one centity instance
- [nf.spawning](nf.spawning.md): Natural spawning (a centity's `spawning` block in `centity.json`): conditions a script decides, which a `spawning` block names with `when`
- [nf.particles](nf.particles.md): The project's particle effects (`particles/<id>/effect.json`): timelines of particles authored in the editor, played at a place by scripts
- [Effect](effect.md): One playing particle effect, from `nf.particles.play`
- [nf.cutscenes](nf.cutscenes.md): The project's cutscenes (`cutscenes/<id>.json`): camera paths keyed in the editor, played for one player at a time
- [Cutscene](cutscene.md): One cutscene playing for one player, from `nf.cutscenes.play`

## Screens

Walls of maps scripts draw on and play videos on.

- [nf.screens](nf.screens.md): Screens: walls of maps, 128 by 128 pixels each, that scripts draw on (pixels, shapes, text, pictures) and play videos on
- [Screen](screen.md): A screen: maps (each 128 by 128 pixels) side by side, which scripts draw on and play videos on, shown in item frames (`place`, or the file's `place`) or as map items in players' hands (`item`)
- [Playback](playback.md): A video playing on a screen, from `screen:play`

## Players and entities

Players, mobs and every other entity, and what's on a player's screen.

- [nf.players](nf.players.md): Players: everyone online, or anyone who has ever joined
- [Player](player.md): Someone on the server: a `Living`, with everything living entities have, and more
- [nf.bots](nf.bots.md): Bots: fake players that scripts join to the server and drive, for opponents and teammates in games, crowds, and anything a player does that an NPC can't
- [Bot](bot.md): A fake player a script drives (see `nf.bots`): a `Player` with everything players have, and the controls a player's client has
- [Entity](entity.md): Something in a world that isn't a block: an arrow, a minecart, a dropped item, a mob, a player
- [Living](living.md): A living entity: a mob, an animal, an armour stand, a player
- [Mob](mob.md): A mob: a `Living` with AI, like a zombie, a cow or a bat
- [Mannequin](mannequin.md): A figure that looks like a player, for shopkeepers, quest givers and statues: a `Living` with a player's skin, a line of text under its name, and a pose, that isn't a player (it's on no player list, counts towards nothing and loads no chunks) and costs no more than an armour stand
- [DroppedItem](droppeditem.md): An item lying on the ground, which players pick up by walking over it: an `Entity` holding one stack
- [Hud](hud.md): One player's HUD: the elements of the project's resource packs (`hud` in `pack.json`: bars, rows of icons, lines of text, each at its place on the screen), shown with what a script sets here
- [Sidebar](sidebar.md): The panel of lines at the right of one player's screen, from `player:sidebar()`: up to 15 lines of MiniMessage under a title, without the score numbers vanilla shows
- [nf.bossbars](nf.bossbars.md): Boss bars: bars across the top of players' screens
- [BossBar](bossbar.md): A bar across the top of players' screens, made by `nf.bossbars.create`
- [nf.teams](nf.teams.md): The project's scoreboard teams: prefixes and suffixes on names, name colours and glow colours, friendly fire, name tags and collision
- [Team](team.md): A scoreboard team, made by `nf.teams.create`: what goes before and after its members' names (over their heads and in the player list), the colour of those names and of their glow, whether members can hurt each other, see each other while invisible, see name tags and push each other

## Worlds and blocks

Worlds, blocks, the project's own blocks and structures.

- [nf.worlds](nf.worlds.md): The server's worlds: finding them, and making, loading and copying them
- [World](world.md): A world on the server (the overworld, the nether, the end, or another the server loads)
- [WorldBorder](worldborder.md): A border: the wall at the edge of a square area, which players can't walk through and which hurts them outside it
- [Block](block.md): One block position in one world
- [nf.blocks](nf.blocks.md): The project's blocks (`blocks/<id>/`): blocks of its own, drawn by its resource pack, with their own hardness, drops and sounds, held in the world as states of the game's blocks (their carriers: note blocks, tripwire, leaves)
- [ProjectBlock](projectblock.md): A project block from `blocks/<id>/block.json`: `this` in the block's script, and what `nf.blocks.get` hands out
- [CustomBlock](customblock.md): A block of the project's own at a position, which is a `Block` like any other: it reads the world live, so one kept from earlier turns into whatever is there now (`block:custom()` says whether it still is one)
- [nf.structures](nf.structures.md): Structures: saved boxes of blocks that `world:place_structure` places

## Items and inventories

Items, the project's own items, inventories, recipes and loot.

- [nf.items](nf.items.md): The project's items (`items/<id>/`): item kinds of its own, whose stacks the server can always tell apart from any other stack of the same Minecraft kind
- [ProjectItem](projectitem.md): A project item from `items/<id>/item.json`: `this` in the item's script, and what `nf.items.get` hands out
- [Inventory](inventory.md): A real inventory: a player's (`player:inventory()`), their ender chest, a storage of the project's that they keep (`player:storage(name, size)`), a container block's (`block:inventory()`: a chest, a barrel, a hopper, a furnace) or an entity's (a chest boat, a donkey, a villager)
- [nf.recipes](nf.recipes.md): The project's recipes: those in `recipes/<id>.json`, and those scripts register
- [nf.loot](nf.loot.md): Loot tables: the project's own (`loot/<id>.json`) and the game's

## Menus and dialogs

Chest menus and dialog screens.

- [nf.menus](nf.menus.md): The project's menus (`menus/<id>/`), and menus scripts make
- [Menu](menu.md): A live menu window from `menus/<id>/`: `this` in the menu's script, and what `player:open_menu`, `nf.menus.shared` and every menu event hand out
- [Slot](slot.md): One slot of one menu window, from `menu:slot(index)` (`this:slot(index)` in the menu's script)
- [MenuTemplate](menutemplate.md): A menu made by a script with `nf.menus.create` rather than read from `menus/<id>/`: what a window opened from it starts as
- [nf.dialogs](nf.dialogs.md): The project's dialogs (`dialogs/<id>/`), and dialogs scripts make
- [Dialog](dialog.md): A dialog from `dialogs/<id>/`: `this` in the dialog's script, and what `nf.dialogs.get` returns
- [Button](button.md): One button of a dialog, from `dialog:button(key)` (`this:button(key)` in the dialog's script)

## Values and utilities

Vectors and locations, text, looks, time, randomness and maths.

- [Vec3](vec3.md): Three numbers: a position, an offset, a velocity, a direction or a scale
- [Location](location.md): A position in a particular world, with an optional facing
- [nf.text](nf.text.md): Helpers for the MiniMessage text players see: escaping what players typed, stripping tags, resource pack glyphs, moving the cursor, and measuring
- [nf.looks](nf.looks.md): Resource pack looks (item models, glyphs, skins, tooltips, equipment looks, sounds) handed from one package's code to another's
- [nf.time](nf.time.md): Dates and durations as text, in the same unit as `nf.server.unix_time()`: milliseconds
- [nf.random](nf.random.md): Randomness `math.random` doesn't give: generators of your own that repeat for a seed, smooth noise, and random ids
- [Random](random.md): A random generator from `nf.random.new`: numbers that repeat for its seed, apart from `math.random` and every other generator
- [nf.math](nf.math.md): Small arithmetic `math` doesn't have, for animating by hand: blending, clamping, rescaling and easing
- [nf.json](nf.json.md): JSON text to and from Lua values

## Files, data, the web and computation

Files, databases, web requests both ways, other plugins and WebAssembly modules.

- [nf.files](nf.files.md): Files in the one directory scripts may keep things in: the only state a script has that survives a restart
- [File](file.md): A path in the scripts' data directory (`plugins/NetherForge/data/`, on the editor's dev server too)
- [Database](database.md): A database, from `nf.db()` or `nf.db('network')`
- [nf.http](nf.http.md): Requests to web services (a Discord webhook, a status API)
- [HttpStream](httpstream.md): A streamed HTTP response, from `nf.http.stream`: its `open`, each `message` and its one `end` are events on it
- [WebSocket](websocket.md): A WebSocket, from `nf.http.websocket`: `send` text on it, and hear its `open`, each `message` and its one `end` as events
- [nf.web](nf.web.md): Web requests to the server: webhooks from stores, CI and chat services, "log in with…" callbacks, small pages and JSON for a companion site
- [Route](route.md): A route a script answers, from `nf.web.route`
- [WebResponse](webresponse.md): How a route's handler answers its request: once, with `send`, `json` or `redirect`, during the handler or later (from a task, or a callback)
- [OAuthFlow](oauthflow.md): A "log in with…" flow, from `nf.web.oauth`: `begin` a login for a player, and hear its `complete` or `fail`
- [nf.economy](nf.economy.md): Players' money, as the server's economy plugin keeps it, through [Vault](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/vault.34315/): whichever economy is registered with it (EssentialsX, CMI, …) answers, so a project never names one
- [nf.placeholders](nf.placeholders.md): Placeholders, through [PlaceholderAPI](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/placeholderapi.6245/): fill in the `%player_name%`-style placeholders every plugin offers, and offer your own as `%<namespace>_<key>%` to every plugin that reads them (scoreboards, chat formats, holograms)
- [nf.wasm](nf.wasm.md): Heavy computation in WebAssembly: a chess engine, pathfinding over a big grid, noise, compression, a library compiled from C, C++ or Rust
- [WasmInstance](wasminstance.md): An instance of a WebAssembly module, from `nf.wasm.instantiate`: its own memory, kept from call to call, so a function can build state another reads
- [WasmProcess](wasmprocess.md): A program started with `nf.wasm.start`: `send` it lines and hear each line it prints as `output`, then its one `end`

## Networks

The other servers behind the same proxy: messages, requests, shared maps, who is where, sending players.

- [nf.network](nf.network.md): The other servers of the network this one is part of: a proxy (Velocity) running NetherForge's proxy plugin, which is the network's hub, and the servers behind it, each running NetherForge and connected to the hub (`network:` in their `config.yml`)
- [NetworkChannel](networkchannel.md): A channel of the network, from `nf.network.channel`: publish on it with `publish`, ask one server with `request`, and hear messages and requests as its `message` and `request` events
- [NetworkMap](networkmap.md): A map the whole network shares, from `nf.network.map`: string keys, any values

## Testing

What `*_test.lua` files run on.

- [nf.test](nf.test.md): What a test file runs on

## Terrain scripts

The separate API a terrain generator script gets.

- [Terrain scripts](terrain-scripts.md): what a terrain generator script can call

## Globals

| Global | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nf` | [`nf`](nf.md) | The NetherForge API: events, timers, tasks and saved data, and a namespace under it for each part of the server (`nf.players`, `nf.worlds`, …; see `nf` for them all). |
| `require` | `fun(name: string): any` | Loads a project module or one of its files, or a file beside a resource's script, and returns what it returned. `require("greeter")` is `modules/greeter/init.lua`; `require("greeter.messages")` is `modules/greeter/messages.lua`. The caller's own files come first: inside a module, its own (`require("util")`); in a centity's, menu's, dialog's or item's script, the `.lua` files in the script's folder (`require("helpers")` in `centities/tower/script.lua` is `centities/tower/helpers.lua`, or `helpers/init.lua`). A module runs once: everyone who requires it gets the running one, state and all. A file beside a script runs as part of it, once per copy of the script, with its globals and its `this`: each centity instance, menu window and dialog has its own. Requiring the script's own file, a circular require, or anything outside the project's Lua is an error. |
| `log` | `fun(...: any)` | Writes a line to the server console (and the editor's, with the file and line it came from). Arguments are converted with `tostring` and joined with tabs. |
| `print` | `fun(...: any)` | The same as `log`. |
| `vec3` | `vec3` | Builds a `Vec3`: `vec3(x, y, z)`. Also holds the common vectors (`vec3.zero`, `vec3.up`, `vec3.north`, …) and `vec3.from_yaw_pitch`. |

## Types

Names the reference uses for a plain Lua type that means more than it.

| Type | Is a | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Text` | `string` | MiniMessage a player reads, like `"<green>Done!"`: a string. A `<glyph:pack/key>` tag in it names a glyph the way the script's own files would: one of its own package's resource packs bare, or `<glyph:namespace:pack/key>` for one a package it depends on exports. The tag means that glyph wherever and whenever the text is shown, whoever shows it; one naming a glyph the script can't use draws nothing, and the server log says why. Text handed back to a script names its glyphs the same way. |

## The Lua standard library

Also there from Lua itself: `string`, `table`, `math`, `utf8`, `coroutine`, `pairs`, `ipairs`, `pcall`, `error`, `tostring`, `tonumber`, `type`, `select`, `setmetatable` and the rest of the basics. The shared library tables are read-only.

`math.random` is seeded afresh each time the server starts the project's scripts (at server start, and on a full reload), so its numbers differ from run to run. Every script shares the one generator: `math.randomseed(n)` gives a repeatable sequence, for every script at once. For a generator of your own, see [`nf.random`](nf.random.md).

Taken away, because they could reach the machine or escape the limits: `io`, `os`, `package`, `load`, `loadstring`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `debug`, `collectgarbage`, `warn`, `java`. Files go through [`nf.files`](nf.files.md), and `require` reaches only the project's own Lua.

Each call into a script runs under an instruction budget, so a runaway loop is stopped with an error instead of freezing the server.

## Requirements

Some functions only work once the project has declared that it uses them, so whoever runs it sees in one place what it may do. Calling one without is an error saying what to declare; the editor marks such a call.

| Requirement | Lets scripts | Declared with | Functions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | keep a database of the package's own | `"requires": { "db": true }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.db`](nf.md#db) |
| `moderation` | ban and unban players, change the whitelist and the server settings players see | `"requires": { "moderation": true }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.server.set_max_players`](nf.server.md#set_max_players), [`nf.server.set_motd`](nf.server.md#set_motd), [`nf.server.set_whitelist_enabled`](nf.server.md#set_whitelist_enabled), [`player:ban`](player.md#ban), [`player:unban`](player.md#unban), [`player:set_whitelisted`](player.md#set_whitelisted) |
| `bots` | join fake players to the server and drive them, when the server owner allows bots | `"requires": { "bots": true }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.bots.join`](nf.bots.md#join), [`nf.bots.all`](nf.bots.md#all), [`bot:leave`](bot.md#leave), [`bot:walk_to`](bot.md#walk_to), [`bot:stop`](bot.md#stop), [`bot:look_at`](bot.md#look_at), [`bot:jump`](bot.md#jump), [`bot:set_sneaking`](bot.md#set_sneaking), [`bot:set_sprinting`](bot.md#set_sprinting), [`bot:chat`](bot.md#chat), [`bot:attack`](bot.md#attack), [`bot:interact`](bot.md#interact), [`bot:use_item`](bot.md#use_item), [`bot:release_item`](bot.md#release_item), [`bot:swing`](bot.md#swing), [`bot:use_block`](bot.md#use_block), [`bot:break_block`](bot.md#break_block), [`bot:swap_hands`](bot.md#swap_hands), [`bot:drop_item`](bot.md#drop_item), [`bot:click_slot`](bot.md#click_slot), [`bot:respawn`](bot.md#respawn) |
| `plugin:vault` | use another plugin on the server | `"requires": { "plugins": ["vault"] }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.economy.balance`](nf.economy.md#balance), [`nf.economy.deposit`](nf.economy.md#deposit), [`nf.economy.withdraw`](nf.economy.md#withdraw) |
| `plugin:placeholderapi` | use another plugin on the server | `"requires": { "plugins": ["placeholderapi"] }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.placeholders.parse`](nf.placeholders.md#parse), [`nf.placeholders.register`](nf.placeholders.md#register) |
| `http` | make requests to other servers, only to the hosts the package lists | each host it calls in `"requires": { "http": [...] }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.http.request`](nf.http.md#request), [`nf.http.stream`](nf.http.md#stream), [`nf.http.websocket`](nf.http.md#websocket) |
| `web` | answer web requests to the server under the package's own path | `"requires": { "web": true }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.web.route`](nf.web.md#route), [`nf.web.url`](nf.web.md#url), [`nf.web.oauth`](nf.web.md#oauth) |
| `wasm` | run the package's WebAssembly modules, off the main thread within the server owner's limits | `"requires": { "wasm": true }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.wasm.functions`](nf.wasm.md#functions), [`nf.wasm.instantiate`](nf.wasm.md#instantiate), [`nf.wasm.run`](nf.wasm.md#run), [`nf.wasm.start`](nf.wasm.md#start) |
| `network` | talk to the other servers of the network the server is part of, and send players between them | `"requires": { "network": true }` in `netherforge.json` | [`nf.network.server_name`](nf.network.md#server_name), [`nf.network.is_connected`](nf.network.md#is_connected), [`nf.network.servers`](nf.network.md#servers), [`nf.network.players`](nf.network.md#players), [`nf.network.find_player`](nf.network.md#find_player), [`nf.network.channel`](nf.network.md#channel), [`nf.network.map`](nf.network.md#map), [`nf.network.send_player`](nf.network.md#send_player) |

## Editor support

The NetherForge editor completes, documents and checks every name here as you type. In another editor, lua-language-server does the same with the stubs the editor writes into each project: see [Editing outside the editor](../guide/external-editors.md#lua-luals-stubs).
